items.title: Claude proves Fermat's Last Theorem
points: Anthropic's Claude formally proved Fermat's Last Theorem, a centuries-old math puzzle unsolved since 1665, over 11 days working mostly autonomously, part of a broader 358-day effort.
Multiple Claude AI agents generated 13 million lines of code (5x larger than Mathlib, a shared mathematics library) and produced 30,000+ supporting theorems as stepping stones.
A coordination tool called Prove2Me gave each agent a live task list to prevent duplicate work; Imperial College London's Kevin Buzzard peer-reviewed and verified the final proof's correctness.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra launches on top ChatGPT plans
points: GPT-6 Astra rolls out immediately to ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with Plus and Business users getting access in following days.
Standard Astra offers roughly half the message allowance per five-hour window compared to GPT-5.6 Sol: Plus users get ~5–45 messages vs. Sol's 10–100.
Free and Go tier subscribers get neither model; developers can access Astra via OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock, counted against existing plan quotas.

items.title: Top 1% of customers drive 80% of AI revenue
points: Ramp's analysis finds the top 1% of customers generate 80% of enterprise revenue at both OpenAI and Anthropic, an unprecedented concentration not seen in other software categories.
At Anthropic, coding tools Cursor and GitHub Copilot alone drove approximately $1.2 billion of the company's $5 billion total annual revenue.
Usage-based pricing (where spending scales with software usage rather than just seat count) amplifies this concentration, creating revenue stability risk if top customers cut back.

items.title: Judge blocks 'Twitter' name reuse; Tweet.app launches
points: A Delaware federal judge ruled for Elon Musk's X, blocking startup Operation Bluebird from using the "Twitter" name for its social network.
The same court found X had abandoned two related trademarks—the word "tweet" and the Twitter bird logo—allowing the startup to rebrand as Tweet.app.
Tweet.app launched publicly after over 172,000 users pre-registered for handles at $20 per reservation during presale, generating funds to help cover legal costs.

items.title: US and China plan AI safety talks
points: The US and China plan their first dedicated AI safety talks in mid-September, focusing on model self-governance and preventing AI-driven cyberattacks.
Talks will also address US concerns about model distillation (a technique where cheaper AI systems learn from larger, more capable ones) being used by Chinese labs.
